_comment: The batch gate-off tool gate-off'd with the single-mutation harness (#3905). Run from a COPY of the files it names so nothing in your checkout is ever mutated: copy scripts/gate_off.py, scripts/gate_off_batch.py, this file, tests/__init__.py, tests/git_env.py, docs/testing-strategy.md and tests/unit/test_gate_off_batch_3905.py into a scratch directory with the same layout, then `python scripts/gate_off.py scripts/gate-off-batch-selfcheck.json` there (about 10-15 minutes). Surviving mutants are listed in the PR; an equivalent mutant or two mechanisms shadowing each other are expected to be named, not hidden. The RSS ceiling the fixtures hand the tool (300 MB) is the only memory bound mutated indirectly: no mutation here removes the bound itself, which belongs to gate_off.py and is pinned by tests/unit/test_gate_off_3714.py.

mutations.label: attribution: an ambiguous failure is handed to its first claimant instead of being re-run
attribution: a failure nobody claims no longer forces a re-run (the rest are declared survivors)
attribution: a contested failure no longer forces a re-run of its claimants
attribution: a survivor of the batch is re-run alone anyway
attribution: an empty name claims every failure
mutations.old: if any(name and name in failure.text for name in mutation.names):
mutations.new: if any(name in failure.text for name in mutation.names):

mutations.label: attribution: declared test-id patterns are ignored
mutations.old: return any(re.search(pattern, failure.id) for pattern in mutation.test_ids)

mutations.label: attribution: a component alone no longer names its site
mutations.old: if component and not names and not test_ids:

batch: a batch that did not collect is attributed instead of re-run member by member
